name: glám dícenn

attributes.attribute: Irish ritual posture for casting a curse
required standing on one leg with one arm out and one eye closed
king cursed through the glám dícenn
sacred vows broken by King Conaire

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: In ancient Ireland a bard or druid used a ritual posture to cast a curse. The posture was called glám dícenn. The caster stood on one leg. He held out one arm and closed one eye. The pose made the curse hard to avoid. A Hag used the glám dícenn against King Conaire. She cursed him for breaking his sacred vows, called geis. The story appears in Da Derga's Hostel.

okr.objective: Explain glám dícenn as the Irish ritual posture used to intensify a curse.
key_results: A bard or druid used the glám dícenn to cast a curse.
The posture used one leg, one arm, and one closed eye.
A Hag used it to curse King Conaire in Da Derga's Hostel.
